the post smolt period growth of Atlantic salmon Salmon salar in the Drammen River was negatively correlated to pre fishery abundance.
post smolt growth in the Atlantic salmon population of the Drammen River has declined since 1983.
post smolt growth decreased throughout the study and that growth was most affected during the fourth and five months of the post smolting year.

the post smolt period of Atlantic salmon Salo salar.
the effects of the post smolts growth on the pre fishery return abundance of Atlantic salmon in Norway.
the growth history of Atlantic salmon Salo salar in the Drammen River and the possible effects of environmental change on growth, and hence on the population.

there is a decline in growth of all three maturation groups, and that this decline may be related to the declining abundance in Norway.
the decline in the abundance of one and sea winter fish returning to the river is a consequence of a decline in post smolt growth, which in turn is a consequence of environmental factors at sea.
the decline in the abundance of Atlantic salmon in the Norwegian rivers has been caused by a combination of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the post smolt phase is a critical time in the life of an Atlantic salmon and is an important time to target with management actions.
post smolt growth is negatively correlated with pre fishery abundance.
the post smolt period is an important period for Atlantic salmon, and that the post smolts are more vulnerable to environmental factors than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a strong relationship between post smolt growth in the fourth and fifth monthly growth indices and the pre fishery return numbers of one and two year old fish to the Drammen river, Norway.
the growth of Atlantic salmon during the fourth month at sea has a major influence on the subsequent survival and return numbers.
post smolt growth is a good indicator of future returns of Atlantic salmon.
